evidence: Read the entire named spec. Its line 108 expressly requires fetched-bundle reconstruction to keep submit validation stable across other workers' arrivals; the visibility section allows concurrent chunk workers. Searched that spec for snapshot/fetched/clock/timestamp/cutoff/boundary/commit/membership/capture/persist/monotonic/tie and equivalent ordering language. The sequence-order and stable-ID guarantees concern source/transition folding and final record ownership, not the set of blocks visible when a worker fetched. No captured block membership, commit watermark, equal-timestamp exclusion, or clock-order constraint supplies the missing snapshot boundary. The spec's explicit accepted parallelism limit is for model-discovered agent work, not deterministic human entries or fetched-bundle stability. Checking the existing machinery expressly referenced by line 108 confirms the premise: src/store/summary.rs load_level0_records (lines 574-590) filters blocks by created_at<=fetched_at; bundle_fold (lines 1173-1181) uses that filter; fetch writes now.0 to fetched_at (lines 1334-1347); insert_block writes now.0 to created_at (lines 1382-1404); submit rebuilds the bundle with the original fetched_at (lines 1538-1547). A block inserted after B fetched with created_at equal to or below B's fetched_at therefore passes the reconstruction filter although absent at B's fetch. The current validator (src/summary/validate.rs lines 166-176) refuses transitions whose rebuilt target is already closed. Under the proposed deterministic seeding, A can close an earlier classified source after B fetched but before B submits; an equal-timestamp A commit then changes B's reconstructed Open target to Resolved and rejects B's otherwise valid later resolution. This is material to the spec's stated stability contract, not a demand beyond its scope. The proposed B-before-A submission test does not exercise the offending intervening-commit order or timestamp tie. A persisted block membership/commit boundary or verified strictly ordered snapshot mechanism is needed; no tests were run or implementation changed.
